clue.text: Primate taking years off heckler with nuclear fission

indicators.note: taking ... off means removing something, here a letter from the heckler word
with taking, off says the years letter is removed
fission is splitting apart, so the heckler word is split open to let a letter in

parts.note: a boo-boy is a jeering heckler, especially at a football ground

explanation.surface: An ape, rid of its years, is pictured with a heckler and atomic splitting — a nonsense scene of science and jeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fission' splits BOOBOY to admit N, giving BONOBOY; 'taking years off' then removes Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The bonobo is a great ape, so it is a kind of primate.

clue.text: Muscle records overwritten by pen

indicators.note: in a down answer, written over means the pen comes on top of the records

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: Someone scribbles over record sleeves with a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm.

clue.text: 'I've trouble networking,' author scrawled with pen

indicators.note: scrawled means written messily, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author scribbles with a pen about difficulty making contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'networking' is not about meeting people: it is the network of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuropath is a person with a disorder of the nervous system, the body's nerve network.

clue.text: On the square is rising socialist Prime Minister

indicators.note: on in a down answer means placed above what follows
rising in a down answer means the word reads upwards

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, Britain's socialist party
a square has four sides

explanation.surface: A socialist is rising to become Prime Minister while staying honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the square' looks like the idiom for honest; it is the four sides of a square. Balfour was in fact a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was the British head of government from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: Giver of terrible hammering entitled man to claim very nearly six counties

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the title wraps round what follows

parts.note: Mr is the title given to a man

indicators.note: nearly means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: jolly is British slang for very, as in jolly good
the six counties is a name for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A titled man lays claim to most of Northern Ireland and hands out a terrible beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The six counties' is a common British name for Northern Ireland. 'Giver of terrible hammering' is Thor's hammer from Norse myth, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mjollnir is the hammer of the Norse god Thor, an instrument that dealt fearsome blows.

clue.text: One's only identity, nevertheless

parts.note: just means only, as in just one
identity is being exactly alike, the same

explanation.surface: Someone's only identity counts all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning even so, used like however or anyway.

clue.text: Sizable vessel, the Bounty?

parts.note: large means sizable
SS is steamship, a prefix for a vessel

explanation.surface: A big ship, perhaps the famous Bounty of the mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty looks like the ship; it is bounty meaning generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving, a synonym for bounty in its sense of liberality.

clue.text: Subduing a force in a disorganised mess

indicators.note: subduing means holding something down, so the jumbled letters hold the other pieces in
disorganised means put out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military force is brought under control in a chaotic canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The NAAFI runs canteens and shops for the British armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is where service people eat, and the NAAFI provides such canteens.

clue.text: New idea ______ had for degeneration?

indicators.note: new says the letters of degeneration are arranged afresh, holding the other word too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist had a new idea that would explain decay.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DEGENERATION, with IDEA taken out, rearrange into the name for the blank. 'had for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Roentgen, discoverer of X-rays, is the scientist who fills the gap as the one who had a new idea.

clue.text: King of the nursery's wrapping up item

indicators.note: wrapping means going round, so the king's name encloses the other word

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nursery rhyme king is wrapping a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' is not an object here: it is the gossip word for two people in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic partners known to be together are called an item, informal for a pair or twosome.

clue.text: Series of unique characters rue joining Mensa for another spell

indicators.note: spell means to write out letters, so another spell rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regrets joining the high-IQ society Mensa for a second stint.
explanation.definitionFit: A login name is a string of characters that nobody else on the system can share.

clue.text: (Issued quarterly) copy@hotmail circulating, given priority

indicators.note: given priority says the wrapped piece comes before the at symbol
circulating means going round, so the mail word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: post is a British word for mail
taken as written
the @ symbol is read as at

explanation.surface: A copy of a quarterly newsletter is circulated by email with high priority.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Issued quarterly)' says the email address is split into its four parts, copy, @, hot and mail, which are then reordered. The bracket only adds disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A photostat is a photographic duplicate of a document, the old trade name for a photocopy.

clue.text: To name some lurker, browser, troll and router shot kneecap to pieces

indicators.note: shot to pieces means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangland list: a lurker, a hood, a troll and a robber shoot someone's kneecap to bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words look like villains; they are internet terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing jargon includes terms such as these for web users and network devices.

clue.text: Sextet given shocking treatment outside bar

indicators.note: outside means the treatment letters sit round the six

parts.note: ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A band of six musicians gets electrified in the street outside a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone from a place is to throw them out of it or exclude them.

clue.text: Jiminy's heart drops, tries repeatedly to run it up?

definitions.text: tries repeatedly to run it up?

parts.note: Jiminy Cricket, Pinocchio's conscience, is a cricket, so his is a cricket's
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Jiminy Cricket's heart sinks as he tries again and again to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsmen score by running between the wickets, so repeated runs are how a total is built up.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the tally is made of runs, so repeated tries to run build that total.

clue.text: 9 playing up earned furious battle in Belgium

parts.note: the answer to 9 across is a pair, and a duo is a pair

indicators.note: furious means wild, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A misbehaving couple are angry about what they earned.

clue.text: Clubs seeking win

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the clubs suit in cards
on a quest means seeking

explanation.surface: Football clubs are looking for a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a victory or winning, especially of territory or someone's affections.

clue.text: In fuzzy broadcast, 15 found it wonderful!

parts.note: the answer to 15 down, the Belgian battle site

explanation.surface: Listening to a crackly radio report of the battle, someone was enthralled.
explanation.definitionFit: Making noises of delight and admiration means you were impressed and thought something marvellous.

clue.text: Colourful shirt — and twice turned up worn by king

parts.note: the printed long dash is named dash

indicators.note: worn by means carried by, so the king letter sits inside
twice means the upright stroke is used two times

parts.note: a dash stood upright on its end is a vertical stroke like the letter I
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A colourful shirt, worn by a king who has twice turned up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The typographical dash in the clue gives DASH; stood on end it is I, so 'twice turned up' is II with K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The dashiki is a loose, brightly patterned West African tunic top.

clue.text: Overuse a place in east London

definitions.meaning: to make something trite by overusing it
a borough in the East End of London

explanation.definitionFit: To hackney a phrase is to wear it out, and Hackney is also a north-east London borough.

clue.text: 'Softly, softly' lion's caged, under a Syrian city

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
p is the musical mark for soft, so twice gives pp

explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, one of the oldest continually inhabited.

clue.text: Even Jack's in, we hear!

clue.text: The compiler owned up over state
